name: Comparison table
summary: One comparison table in five forms: two, three (with or without a highlighted column), four and five compared columns beside a feature column. Rows are grouped under a pink group heading; each cell is a tick, a cross or a short text value. Two and three columns stay a table on a phone; four and five scroll sideways with the feature column held in place. It shares the Pricing Large table's row, group and highlight styles, without prices or buttons in the header.
highlights: Five layouts on one page, each with its own labelled preview and paste-and-run snippet
A real <table> with a caption, column and row headers, and grouped rows (th scope="colgroup"), so a screen reader reads each cell with its feature and column
Tick and cross cells are <aha-icon> system-check (Vivid Pink) and system-x (muted) with a visually hidden Yes or No; text cells hold a short value
The highlighted column is the Pricing Large table's 2 px Vivid Pink outline with a Recommended <aha-tag>; drop the aha-comparison__col--highlight classes for a neutral table
Phone: two and three columns stay a table (36% feature column, 14 px cells, column descriptions hidden); four and five scroll sideways inside a focusable region with the feature column sticky
Same header (eyebrow, h2 title, lead), 48 px call-to-action gap and gutters (64, 24 and 16 px) as the other Marketing sections, ending with one Sign up call to action
Each section is a container-query block: it steps down at 767 px and tightens again below 480 px, wherever it sits
layoutsIntro: Each section is one comparison table. They share one set of class names (aha-comparison), so the base CSS is pasted once; the four and five column layouts add aha-comparison--scroll and one min-width rule.

guidance.title: Choosing a comparison table
guidance.intro: Every layout below has a White / Accent switch in its preview and a tab for each in its code.

points.title: By the number of options
points.text: Two columns for a head-to-head page, three for a shortlist, four or five for a roundup. Never more than five compared columns: split a bigger comparison into two tables.

points.title: Highlight one column at most
points.text: Highlight the column you recommend, usually AhaSlides or the most popular plan. Leave every column plain when the reader should choose freely.

points.title: Cells
points.text: Use a tick or a cross for yes or no, and a short value ("Unlimited", "100") when the answer is a number or a level. Keep each value to a few words so the phone table does not wrap into tall rows.

points.title: Rows
points.text: Group rows under three or four short headings and keep each group to five rows or fewer. Put the rows that decide the choice first.

points.title: Background
points.text: White is the default. Add aha-comparison--accent to lay the pale pink Accent background (bgAccent) over white; the table itself stays white.
